visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a female dermatologist, known as Dr. Acne Scar Queen, sitting in a well-lit office setting. She has short, reddish-brown hair and wears circular glasses and a tan sleeveless vest. Behind her, professional certifications and a YouTube play button are visible, establishing her authority in the medical field. (2) The scene cuts to a close-up demonstration of a medical laser procedure. A white laser handpiece, clearly marked with the brand name MultiFrax, is moved over skin affected by reddish stretch marks. Bright flashes of light occur at the point of contact, illustrating the treatment's interaction with the tissue in a clinical environment. (3) Transitioning back to the office, the doctor continues her explanation, gesturing with her hands to emphasize her points. Large, colorful text overlays in Traditional Chinese highlight key terms like 'stretch marks', while the lighting remains consistent, bright, and professional, focusing on her facial expressions and communication style. (4) A digital animation illustrates the underlying technology. A cross-section of the skin layers is shown being penetrated by two distinct laser wavelengths: Thulium 1921nm and 1550nm. These beams are depicted as cyan lines reaching different depths, providing a technical visual aid to complement the doctor's verbal narrative about deep tissue repair. (5) The visual narrative shifts to show the laser being used for facial acne scars on a different patient. The patient lies horizontally with protective eye covers while the doctor precisely applies the laser. This demonstrates the versatility of the MultiFrax machine across different clinical applications and skin conditions. (6) A macro close-up image displays a healing face with small, brownish scabs arranged in a grid-like pattern. A white dashed circle highlights the treated area, and text explains that this is a normal post-treatment phase. The image provides realistic expectations for recovery, contrasting with the earlier clinical procedure shots. (7) The doctor concludes the video in her office, leaning forward slightly towards the camera. She summarizes the benefits of the dual-wavelength approach. The video then transitions to a final white brand card featuring the 'DRX Dermatology Clinic' logo, contact numbers, and social media handles in clean, professional typography.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A female voice with a clear, professional Mandarin accent begins the narration. She speaks at a moderate pace with a friendly yet authoritative tone. In the background, a light and upbeat acoustic guitar track plays, providing a steady rhythmic foundation with a major tonality and simple percussion elements. (2) A short, airy 'whoosh' sound effect triggers a new phase as the visual cuts to the procedure demonstration. The narrator's voice remains constant in volume and pitch, seamlessly continuing her explanation of the laser treatment process. The background music continues without interruption, maintaining a consistent energy level. (3) As technical details are discussed, the speaker's articulation remains sharp and highly enunciated for clarity. The acoustic guitar BGM swells slightly in the mix but remains subservient to the primary vocal track. There are no significant pauses, indicating a well-rehearsed or post-edited narrative flow typical of high-quality informative video content. (4) A soft digital beep or click sound effect is introduced to coincide with the animation of the laser beams penetrating the skin. This sound design choice emphasizes the precision of the medical technology. The narrator explains the specific wavelengths, and her pitch variability increases slightly to maintain engagement. (5) The audio environment shifts as the doctor concludes her talk with a warm and encouraging tone. The acoustic guitar music begins a slow, deliberate fade-out. A final sharp digital transition sound marks the appearance of the end card containing the clinic's contact information and branding.
